overview: This autumn report gives broad commentary only, with few question-by-question details.
Calculations in Section B were generally well done and logically set out; most finished in time though about 1 in 10 omitted 28(b)(ii).
Weaker candidates wrote too much working for numerical MCQs, recalled definitions poorly (e.g. confusing work function with threshold frequency), and left symbols undefined.
Premature rounding and poor recall of unit prefixes (e.g. nano) cost marks.
Stronger candidates used the data booklet well, showed every step in 'show' questions, matched answer length to the marks and used scientific vocabulary precisely.
assessment_for_learning: For numerical MCQs identify the key physics and proportionalities (e.g. v proportional to sqrt(KE)) rather than doing full calculations; eliminate impossible options.
Learn basic physics thoroughly - gaps lead to guessing on simple MCQs.
Use short sentences or bullet points in explanations to avoid contradicting earlier correct statements.
Use the number of marks as a guide to the number of distinct physics points needed.
Underline key terms (e.g. maxima and minima) and reflect before writing.
Use the paper as a mock to practise timing, command words, carrying unrounded values through, and absolute uncertainty.

good_practice: Recognised air resistance rises with speed so the resultant force and acceleration decrease; eliminated graphs with increasing or constant acceleration
Wrote KE = 1/2 mv^2 and energy gained = eV, ruled out a speed decrease, and scaled speed by sqrt(3.5)

common_errors: Stated that total momentum of the system equals the final momentum of the ball
good_practice: Person moves left, conservation of momentum or Newton's third law, total momentum stays zero, person's speed smaller than the ball's
Showed every step leading to the 'show' value
Calculated absolute uncertainty to reach a conclusion from the data

common_errors: Premature rounding leading to wrong final answer
Said the drone was accelerating and still moving upwards at Z
misconceptions: Misreading a negatively sloping v-t section - it means deceleration

common_errors: Gave the amplitude ratio 2.4 instead of 2.4^2 = 5.76
Wrote a fraction on the answer line
misconceptions: Forgetting that intensity is proportional to amplitude squared

common_errors: Described constructive and destructive interference without linking them to the maxima and minima
good_practice: Explained maxima/minima using path or phase difference

misconceptions: Treating threshold frequency and work function as synonyms
good_practice: Explained no emission above lambda0 because each photon's energy is less than the work function

common_errors: Poor recall of the nano prefix
Divided laser power by 1.60 x 10^-19 J instead of the photon energy 4.06 x 10^-19 J
